_about: The one source for every variant of the Palanor skill. build.py renders dist/ from this file, SKILL.body.md, references/ and flows.json; check.py fails CI when dist/ drifts or a tool name or argument is not on the live server.
name: palanor
description: Sourced economic data, indices and charts from Palanor MCP. Finds a U.S. or world data series (rates, the yield curve, jobs, inflation, energy, housing, trade), says where it stands in its own record with dated changes, reads Palanor Custom Indices and Currents, makes a chart or embed, and cites the source and licence from each result's provenance block. Use when the user asks about economic or market data, a Palanor index or Current, or wants a chart of public data with its source.
compatibility: Needs the Palanor MCP server (https://mcp.palanor.com, Streamable HTTP) connected in the agent, signed in with a Palanor account or a Palanor API key sent as an Authorization: Bearer header (free key: https://palanor.com/developers/keys). Needs network access.

agentskills._about: The Agent Skills standard (agentskills.io). Validated with skills-ref. Loads as is in any harness that reads the standard.
setup: ## Before the first call
The tools below come from the Palanor MCP server. If they aren't in your tool list, the server isn't connected:
tell the user to add `{server}` as a remote (Streamable HTTP) MCP server in their agent, signed in with Palanor or
with a key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (a free key takes a minute at {keys_url}). Don't try to reach
the server some other way, and never ask the user to paste a key into the chat.
Some harnesses put a prefix on MCP tool names (`palanor__palanor_get_signal`, `mcp__palanor__palanor_get_signal`).
The names in this skill are the server's own; match them to whatever prefix your tool list shows.

openclaw._about: OpenClaw (tested with openclaw 2026.11.5). Reads the standard; adds metadata.openclaw so `openclaw skills check` reports the missing key. Native MCP: tools appear as palanor__<tool>.
setup: ## Before the first call
In OpenClaw the server's tools appear with the server name in front: `palanor__palanor_get_signal` for
`palanor_get_signal`, and so on. The names in this skill are the server's own; add the `palanor__` prefix when
you call them.
If no `palanor__` tools are in your tool list, the server isn't connected. Tell the user to run:
```bash
openclaw mcp add palanor --url {server} --transport streamable-http \
--header 'Authorization=Bearer ${PALANOR_API_KEY}'
with `PALANOR_API_KEY` set in the Gateway's environment (the shell or `~/.openclaw/.env`; a free key takes a
minute at {keys_url}), then restart the Gateway. Never ask the user to paste a key into the chat.

goose._about: Goose (tested with goose 1.60.1). Reads the standard from ~/.agents/skills; the recipe bundles the MCP extension (header from PALANOR_API_KEY) with the summon extension, which loads skills. Tools appear as palanor__<tool>.
setup: ## Before the first call
In Goose the server's tools appear with the extension name in front: `palanor__palanor_get_signal` for
`palanor_get_signal`, and so on. The names in this skill are the server's own; add the `palanor__` prefix when
you call them.
If no `palanor__` tools are available, the extension isn't enabled. Tell the user to start Goose with the
Palanor recipe (`goose session --recipe palanor.recipe.yaml`, with `PALANOR_API_KEY` set; a free key takes a
minute at {keys_url}), or to add `{server}` as a Remote Extension (Streamable HTTP) with an
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` header in `goose configure`. Never ask the user to paste a key into the chat.

palanor.recipe.yaml: # Goose recipe: the Palanor MCP extension plus the Palanor skill.
# Generated by skills/palanor/tools/build.py from skills/palanor/source. Do not edit by hand.
description: Read Palanor's public data lattice (signals, Custom Indices, Currents, charts) with sources and licences.
Use the palanor extension's tools (named palanor__<tool>) for questions about economic and market data,
Palanor Custom Indices and Currents, and sourced charts. Load the palanor skill first (load_skill) and follow it.
Find slugs with palanor__palanor_search_signals; never guess one. Give every number with its observation date
and every change with both of its dates. Cite each value from its provenance block: the attribution line and the
licence name. A signal the server says is not licensed for redistribution, an embed with embeddable false, or an
index component with latest_value_withheld is display-only on palanor.com: never present it as downloadable,
and never fill in its value from elsewhere.
description: Palanor MCP server (read-only public data lattice)

hermes._about: Hermes Agent (tested with hermes-agent v0.23.2). Reads the standard; adds version, author, required_environment_variables (Hermes asks for the key once and keeps it in ~/.hermes/.env, where the MCP header reads it) and metadata.hermes. Tools appear as mcp__palanor__<tool>.

required_environment_variables.__raw__:
- name: PALANOR_API_KEY
    prompt: "Palanor API key (free at https://palanor.com/developers/keys)"
    help: "https://palanor.com/developers/keys"
    required_for: "the Palanor MCP server's Authorization header"

setup: ## Before the first call
In Hermes the server's tools appear as `mcp__palanor__palanor_get_signal` for `palanor_get_signal`, and so on
(when the server is named `palanor`). The names in this skill are the server's own; add the `mcp__palanor__`
prefix when you call them.
If no `mcp__palanor__` tools are in your tool list, the server isn't connected. Tell the user to add this entry to
the `mcp_servers` section of their Hermes config, then run `/reload-mcp`:
```yaml
mcp_servers:
palanor:
url: "{server}"
headers:
Authorization: "Bearer ${PALANOR_API_KEY}"
Hermes asks the user for `PALANOR_API_KEY` when this skill loads and keeps it out of the chat (a free key takes a
minute at {keys_url}). Never ask the user to paste a key into the chat, and never read or print it.
